title: Sections are invariant under flat quasi-compact maps with connected geometric fibres
statement: Let $f:T\to S$ be a flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and quasi-compact [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] whose geometric fibres [def-weil-geometric-fibre] are connected [def-weil-connected-scheme]. For every sheaf of sets $F$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-of-sets] on the small etale site $S_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], pullback induces a bijection $\Gamma(S,F)\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(T,f^{-1}F)$, where $f^{-1}F$ is the etale inverse image of sheaves of sets [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units].

proof.text: For every point $s$ of $S$, the assumed connected geometric fibre over a geometric point above $s$ is nonempty [def-weil-connected-scheme], so $f$ has a point above $s$ [def-weil-geometric-fibre]. Thus $f$ is surjective. Together with the given flatness and quasi-compactness, the singleton family $\{f:T\to S\}$ is an fpqc covering by [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering]: for an affine open $V\subseteq S$, $f^{-1}V$ is quasi-compact by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], so finitely many affine opens in $f^{-1}V$ cover it and their images cover $V$.

proof.text: Let $\alpha\in\Gamma(T,f^{-1}F)$ and let $s$ be any point of $S$. Choose an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\kappa(s)$ and its geometric point $\bar s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$ [def-weil-geometric-fibre]. Put $T_{\bar s}=T\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$. Let $p:T_{\bar s}\to T$ and $h:T_{\bar s}\to\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ be the projections, so $f\circ p=\bar s\circ h$. By [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units] the restriction $p^{-1}f^{-1}F$ of $f^{-1}F$ to $T_{\bar s}$ is canonically $(\bar s\circ h)^{-1}F$, compatibly with pullback of sections and associatively under further composition (clauses (1), (2)); by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-geometric-fibre-constant-sections] it is the constant sheaf with value $F_{\bar s}$; since this fibre is connected and nonempty, $\alpha|_{T_{\bar s}}$ is the constant section for a unique $a_{\bar s}\in F_{\bar s}$. The fibre of $T\times_ST$ over $\bar s$ is $T_{\bar s}\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\Omega}T_{\bar s}$. Using again the composition isomorphisms of [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units] to identify the restriction to this product fibre of the pullback of $\alpha$ along either projection $T\times_ST\to T$ with the pullback of $\alpha|_{T_{\bar s}}$ along the corresponding projection $T_{\bar s}\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\Omega}T_{\bar s}\to T_{\bar s}$, naturality in [lem-weil-pbc-etale-geometric-fibre-constant-sections] says that both projection pullbacks of $\alpha$ restrict to the constant section with value $a_{\bar s}$ on this product fibre.

proof.text: A geometric point of $T\times_ST$ maps to a point $s$ of $S$ and has an algebraically closed residue field containing $\kappa(s)$ [def-weil-geometric-point]. Choose an embedding of the algebraic closure $\Omega$ used in Step 2 into this field over $\kappa(s)$; the point then factors through the product fibre over $\bar s$. The two projection pullbacks of $\alpha$ agree on that fibre by Step 2; since the germ of a section at a geometric point equals, via the bijection of [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-stalk-germ] for the inclusion $j$ of the product fibre, the germ of its pullback along $j$ at the lifted geometric point, they have equal germs at every geometric point of $T\times_ST$. Equality of sections follows directly from [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks] and the separated part of the sheaf axiom [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-of-sets]: equality of germs supplies an etale neighbourhood of each geometric point on which they agree, these neighbourhoods cover, and the sheaf axiom makes the sections equal. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-etale-sections-fpqc-descent] to the singleton fpqc covering from Step 1 produces a unique section of $F$ on $S$ pulling back to $\alpha$. The same uniqueness proves injectivity of the canonical map.
